### Before upgrading: update every host to v0.6.0

This release changes how hosts talk to each other. v0.6.0 cannot pair or switch with
v0.5.x or earlier, so update every computer sharing the display to v0.6.0. The pairing
password and settings are kept; there is no need to pair again.

### Each computer sets only its own port

You could previously choose, on one computer, which port another added host was plugged
into. Now each computer sets only its own:

- **Added hosts' ports are shown read-only**: each host reports its own, and one that has
  not yet shows "Not reported yet".
- **To change a host's port, set it on that computer.** It is then shared with the others.
- Other hosts can neither change this computer's port nor take the port it is on.

Every host shares one pairing password, so any of them used to be able to point another
host's switch at the wrong input. Now only the port's owner can set it.

### Port settings stay in sync, and a computer that was away catches up

Each host's port setting now carries the time it changed and is kept in sync between hosts:

- **A computer that was off or offline** catches up the next time it connects, and a port
  that was cleared meanwhile is not brought back by old data.
- **Notices that cannot be delivered yet** are kept and retried, and one that keeps failing
  does not hold back the others.
- **Reset displays affects only this computer.** Pressing it on any host used to clear every
  host's port; now it clears only this computer's own.
- A remote update no longer interrupts a menu or input note you are editing; it is applied
  once you leave the field.

### Security hardening

This release follows a full security scan:

- **Talks only to hosts on a local network.** MuxSU accepts connections only from this
  computer, private networks (such as 192.168.x.x and 10.x.x.x), link-local addresses, and
  the 100.64.0.0/10 range used by VPNs such as Tailscale, and connects to nothing else.
- **Limits simultaneous connections**, so a device on the network cannot tie MuxSU up by
  opening a flood of them.
- **Each window can do only what it needs.** The host switcher can switch hosts, but cannot
  reset settings, install updates or send diagnostic reports.
- **Wake-on-LAN MAC addresses are no longer broadcast.** Each host sends its own in signed
  replies, so a forged advertisement cannot send wake packets elsewhere. Wake packets are
  also sent only to the local network.
- **No amount of data from other hosts can stop this one being switched to.** Synced
  data is limited in number and size, and a reply that grows too large drops what can be
  caught up on later, never what switching needs.
- **Sync data dated in the future is ignored.** A setting from another host dated more than a
  minute ahead of this computer's clock is not adopted, so one bad entry cannot override every
  later change.
- **The settings file is replaced whole.** A crash or power cut mid-write no longer leaves a
  damaged file that loses the pairing.
- **Diagnostic reports hide display serial numbers better.** Serials are hashed with a key
  derived from the pairing password, so only hosts in the same pairing can compare them, and
  reports are sent over HTTPS only.
- **The Windows installer**, when removing an old DisplayMux install, runs only the
  uninstaller inside that install's own folder, and never one from a user's folder when
  run as administrator.

### Why the version jumps to 0.6.0

Under rules 1 and 2 in `docs/versioning.md`: upgrading needs every host updated together,
and a v0.5.x host can no longer pair with an updated one. Setting another host's port has
also been removed.

### Known limitations

- Pairing works only over a local network or a VPN in the 100.64.0.0/10 range. A VPN that
  uses other public addresses cannot connect.
- The Wake-on-LAN broadcast address must be on a local network or 255.255.255.255.
- A shared public Wi-Fi network (a café's, say) is also a private network, so other devices
  on it can still see MuxSU, though they cannot control it without the pairing password.
- When the Mac and Windows read different serial numbers from the same display (the Acer
  VG252Q reads one on both, but not the same one), the two hosts treat it as two displays.
  Asking the other host to switch that display for you may report that the shared display
  was not found.
- Unmerging does not move back the input settings and notes that were folded into the other
  identity.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed and not yet notarised with an Apple Developer ID, so
  Gatekeeper may ask you to allow it manually.
